ablations.prompt: Explain inflation Keep it under 60 words. Use 3 bullet points.

runs.answer:
- Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises over time.
- As prices climb, each unit of currency buys fewer goods, reducing purchasing power.
- Central banks typically aim for modest inflation, around 2% annually, to keep the economy stable.

- Inflation is the general rise in prices across an economy over time.
- As prices increase, each unit of money buys fewer goods and services, reducing purchasing power.
- Common causes include higher demand, rising production costs, and expansion of the money supply.

ablations.prompt: Explain inflation to a 10-year-old. Use 3 bullet points.

runs.answer:
- Inflation is when things slowly get more expensive over time. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were little might cost a dollar or more today.

- It means your money buys less than it used to. If you have $5, you can get fewer toys or snacks than you could a few years ago, even though the number on your money hasn't changed.

- Most prices rise a little bit each year, which is normal. Grown-ups who run the country try to keep it slow and steady, because if prices shot up too fast, it would be hard for families to afford everyday things.

- Inflation is when prices go up over time, so the same money buys less stuff. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your parents were kids might cost $1.50 today.

- It usually happens slowly, because lots of people want to buy things and businesses charge a little more to cover their costs, like higher prices for ingredients, wages, and rent.

- Your money doesn't disappear, but it can stretch less far, which is why grown-ups try to earn more money each year so they can keep up with rising prices.
